# Numeric precision

Numeric precision for weights, gradients and matmul kernels. One setting drives the dtype parameters are built in, the precision Lightning steps at (which decides whether gradients are low-precision) and the float32 matmul kernel policy, so the three cannot drift apart. A level the hardware cannot honor is downgraded to the nearest one that runs, with a notice.

Namespace: ``registry.namespace("precision")``, declared in ``praxis.trainers.precision`` (4 entries)

Selected with ``--precision`` (default: ``float32``).

## `bfloat16`

Weights, activations and gradients all in bf16. On a CUDA device that predates bf16
support it is downgraded to float16.

## `float16`

fp16 compute with fp32 master weights and loss scaling. Off CUDA it is downgraded to
bfloat16, since CPU fp16 kernels are largely unimplemented.

## `float32`

fp32 weights and gradients, with TF32 matmul kernels where available.

## `float64`

Double precision end to end, with TF32 kernels off; roughly 1/64 the throughput on
consumer GPUs.
